[Call for Conference Proposals]{.h4}

[**From Evidence to Impact: Translating Psychology-Law Science and Expertise to Advance Justice and Human Rights**]{.event-info}

[Submission deadline: October 15, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. PT]{.event-time}

[{{< fa paper-plane aria-hidden="true" >}} Submit a proposal](https://ap-ls2027.exordo.com/){.btn .btn-primary role="button"}
[{{< fa file-word aria-hidden="true" >}} Download](https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=1S1SpUplrwBA7VAqc8eyl2OxZhFTOe5wm){.btn .btn-outline-primary role="button"}

:::

::: session-description

We are pleased to invite proposal submissions for the AP-LS 2027 Annual Conference through the [Ex Ordo Conference Submission Portal](https://ap-ls2027.exordo.com/). Proposals are due by **October 15, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. PT**. Proposals will be evaluated through a blind review process focused on intellectual merit, innovation, novelty, and integration of multiple aspects of the field.

:::

## Submissions for Special Consideration {.plenary}

::: session-description

We welcome submissions in all areas of psychology-law. However, we particularly encourage proposals that align with the conference theme: **“From Evidence to Impact: Translating Psychology-Law Science and Expertise to Advance Justice and Human Rights.”**

Special consideration will be given to proposals focused on:

1. Settings, issues, and populations particularly vulnerable to human and civil rights violations, such as immigration detention and immigration courts, juvenile justice, false confessions or pleas, and correctional settings.
2. Research that strengthens and advances forensic assessment and treatment practices, particularly with culturally diverse populations.
3. Innovative approaches to effectively communicating and translating psychology-law science and expertise to legal professionals, policymakers, practitioners, and the public.

We encourage you to think creatively about symposium formats and consider submissions that extend beyond traditional research findings and engage with broader issues facing our field. These might include topics of debate that grapple with challenging or contested issues in psychology-law; interdisciplinary work that bridges psychology with other fields and professions operating in the legal system, such as legal scholars, judges, and attorneys; explorations of ethical dilemmas; mock trials that create opportunities for learning and discussion; or case-based presentations that illustrate important issues in research, practice, and policy.

:::

## Submission Requirements {.plenary}

::: session-description

This year’s proposal requirements will be similar to last year’s, including shorter abstract word counts across submission categories. **Data Blitzes are no longer a proposal type for the upcoming conference.** Visual instructions are linked below to clarify and streamline the submission process, particularly for symposium submissions.

Authors will be asked to attest whether they used generative AI in their submission. Use of generative AI does not result in automatic disqualification, but the submission will be routed to reviewers with expertise in generative AI.

:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Submission Details

All proposal materials must be submitted through the [Ex Ordo Conference Submission Portal](https://ap-ls2027.exordo.com/) by **October 15, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. PT**.

To ensure blind review, all proposal materials must be completely anonymized.

[{{< fa paper-plane aria-hidden="true" >}} Open the submission portal](https://ap-ls2027.exordo.com/){.btn .btn-primary role="button"}
:::

## Proposal Types {.plenary}

### Symposium {.session-title}

::: session-description

[Follow the step-by-step symposium submission guide](https://drive.google.com/file/d/19hD5ffa1Y7BmuHD1COhSUdE9vKGp6ljs/view?usp=sharing). **The symposium submission process is different from last year’s process.**

A symposium—called a “panel” in Ex Ordo—is a 60- to 80-minute session with multiple presentations or papers focused on a single topic. It includes an independent discussant or chair and a minimum of three and maximum of five papers.

Symposium submissions occur in two steps:

1. One member of the symposium—preferably the chair or discussant—submits a **1,000-word summary of the overall symposium** using the “Panels” submission type in Ex Ordo.

   - Include three or four learning objectives.
   - List the symposium discussant and/or chair.
   - Add the submitting author of each symposium paper as a “Convener.”
   - Upload the CV or CVs for the discussant and/or chair as a **PDF**.

2. After the overall symposium summary is submitted, the submitting authors listed as Conveners will see the symposium in their “My Panels” list. Each author then uses the “Submit to Panel” button to submit a **400- to 500-word abstract** that concisely explains the purpose and content of the paper.

   - For empirical studies, literature reviews, and meta-analyses, include: *Objectives, Method, Results, Conclusions,* and *Implications*.
   - For case studies and theoretical or methodological studies, include: *Purpose, Description, Assessment,* and *Conclusions*.
   - Include one or two learning objectives.
   - Upload the CV or CVs for the submitting author and all listed co-authors as a **PDF**.

:::

### Paper {.session-title}

::: session-description

[Follow the step-by-step paper submission guide](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1muSb6VDxaLOtPXmNUgmqqh3fGBel6ZBn/view?usp=sharing).

A paper is a presentation describing an individual research topic or piece of legal scholarship. Accepted papers are clustered into 60-minute themed sessions, with three or four papers in each session.

Enter a **400- to 500-word abstract** directly into the Ex Ordo Conference Submission Portal. The abstract should concisely explain the purpose and content of the paper.

- For empirical studies, literature reviews, and meta-analyses, include: *Objectives, Method, Results, Conclusions,* and *Implications*.
- For case studies and theoretical or methodological studies, include: *Purpose, Description, Assessment,* and *Conclusions*.
- Include one or two learning objectives.

:::

### Poster {.session-title}

::: session-description

[Follow the step-by-step poster submission guide](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1muSb6VDxaLOtPXmNUgmqqh3fGBel6ZBn/view?usp=sharing).

A poster is a concise visual summary of research or legal scholarship displayed on a large poster board, such as a 4 × 6-foot board. Accepted posters are presented at one of two evening poster sessions on Friday or Saturday. While not required, presenters are encouraged to follow the [APA Convention Poster Instructions](https://nam02.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fclicks.memberclicks-mail.net%2Fls%2Fclick%3Fupn%3Du001.CxNkYM1Ne08ZaphTIQeWdCE-2BnDJiS7F2EwQx1HWBiOgetYnM5nlsmNvypiUBFzg0H6-2Fu12D8dR-2FezRbPKvliIDHbRlYpD3uDiKBajZDvbZNr1AeaCq54-2BUrxLW12gcxjZmKo_VdB2YlC81qs4b1WUj-2BbY-2Bnn6EjknpMw774PCNt5dKFsYCnWOGNIu4Nv-2BeHtDN5w-2FEVq3tOwCnhfTL0AGEqPk1uYNbfXovt5u6QUMzn6F1bpW1DRqtbTZK2i8C2N99tLR8oTLTZYgjwQOeqB4UoLvuRmMkH4nVhgHPYILG8M14cohq80h49iD3EVCAGoWdmyTDunTG9EOFri-2FAsTGPvUP6D2CW8KYrSppI8xT79hTbskNd58EtZ2LU4D4cYlDco1HgK2JSEwP0o4Lb23TrH9xm3rLyTzJ8dOBYkAqtlBdKnLxM2dXwOZY11vSsekXXXP6fTug8L95r8S13W786Un9Dw-3D-3D&data=05%7C02%7Ccmb472%40connect.rutgers.edu%7Ca92db393263649a6bb7d08ddf2350671%7Cb92d2b234d35447093ff69aca6632ffe%7C1%7C0%7C638933031752987593%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=S16LMJ1CB8PezC5I%2FFJdMiXWRPQpe1QWmm969sdRB44%3D&reserved=0).

## Call for AP-LS 2027 Annual Conference Reviewers {.plenary}

::: session-description

Professional and graduate student reviewers are invited for all content areas. Proposals will be distributed for review in mid-October, and reviews will be due by **November 20, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. PT**.

There are two ways to become a reviewer for the AP-LS 2027 Conference:

- If you are submitting a proposal, indicate your interest in serving as a reviewer during the Ex Ordo submission process. You will later receive an email from Ex Ordo asking you to identify your topical areas of expertise.
- If you are not submitting a proposal—or would like to sign up now—complete the [Reviewer Sign-Up Google Form](https://forms.gle/xvCyX7kcHPohK11k7). You will later receive an email from Ex Ordo asking you to identify your areas of expertise.

[{{< fa clipboard-check aria-hidden="true" >}} Sign up to review](https://forms.gle/xvCyX7kcHPohK11k7){.btn .btn-outline-primary role="button"}

:::

## Call for AP-LS Pre-Conference Workshop Proposals {.plenary}

::: session-description

The AP-LS Continuing Education Committee is accepting proposals for pre-conference workshops at the AP-LS Annual Conference in Louisville, Kentucky. Workshops will take place on **Wednesday, March 17, 2027**, the day before general conference programming begins.

We seek proposals for innovative and cutting-edge topics. Presenters should briefly describe how their proposed workshop promotes equity, inclusion, and justice in psychology and law. Workshop presenters will receive an honorarium commensurate with the workshop length—half-day or full-day.

Proposals are due by **October 15, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. PT** and may be submitted through the [Pre-Conference Workshop Proposal Form](https://forms.gle/uEvcvXPRKQNwFqpH9). Contact Sara Millspaugh, Ph.D., at [ce@ap-ls.org](mailto:ce@ap-ls.org) with questions.

[{{< fa chalkboard-teacher aria-hidden="true" >}} Submit a workshop proposal](https://forms.gle/uEvcvXPRKQNwFqpH9){.btn .btn-primary role="button"}

**Please note:** Pre-conference workshops are separate from general AP-LS conference programming and use separate application portals and review processes. You are welcome to submit proposals both to the Continuing Education Committee for a pre-conference workshop and to the AP-LS Conference Chairs for general conference programming from March 18-20, 2027.

*Sara Millspaugh, Ph.D.<br>
Pronouns: she/her<br>
Chair, AP-LS Continuing Education Committee*

:::
